title: Tensor-triangle two-out-of-three for acyclicity
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal A^\bullet$ an acyclic complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and $K_1^\bullet\to K_2^\bullet$ a morphism of cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with mapping cone $K_3^\bullet$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tensoring the cone sequence with $\mathcal A^\bullet$ identifies the resulting total complex with the mapping cone of the tensor map. If two of the three total tensor complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}K_i^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are acyclic, then the third is acyclic.

source.place: Lemma 07A3 (sites-cohomology-lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three), with the cone description from Definition 06YN

proof.text: Use MonoidalPreadditive from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the zero-morphism preservation instances of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Apply [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], CochainComplex.mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso, and its inr compatibility lemma to identify Tot(A ⊗ Cone(f)) with Cone(Tot(1_A ⊗ f)), including the claimed inclusion equality.

source.place: Lemma 07A3, cone comparison in the proof

proof.text: For g = Tot(1_A ⊗ f), HomotopyCategory.mappingCone_triangleh_distinguished g gives a distinguished cone triangle. By [lem-pc-acyclic-triangle-two-out-of-three], apply ObjectProperty.ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₃, ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₂ and ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₁ to the acyclic subcategory, respectively. Convert subcategory membership to complex acyclicity using quotient_obj_mem_subcategoryAcyclic_iff_acyclic; transport the third vertex along the quotient of the cone comparison isomorphism from Step 1 using prop_iff_of_iso. These are the three desired implications.
